49742.subject: Literature in English
49742.explanation: A Panegyric is a formal public speech, or (in later use) written verse, delivered in high praise of a person or thing, a generally highly studied and undiscriminating eulogy, not expected to be critical.

49745.subject: Literature in English
49745.question_text: A literary work in which the characters are animals is a ____________
49745.explanation: A Fable is a short tale to teach a moral lesson, often with animals or inanimate objects as characters

49747.subject: Literature in English
49747.question_text: A short single act drama is called____________
49747.explanation: A playlet can be definied as a short play or dramatic piece.

49751.subject: Literature in English
49751.question_text:
Through the trees, I'll hear a single

Ringing sound, a cowbell jingle 

The underlined is an example of____________ryhme
49751.explanation: End rhyme is defined as when a poem has lines ending with words that sound the same.

The lines illustrates________

49758.subject: Literature in English
49758.question_text: A play on words for literary effect is_________
49758.explanation:
Pun can be defined as a joke exploiting the different possible meanings of a word or the fact that there are words which sound alike but have different meanings.

synonyms: play on words

49759.subject: Literature in English
49759.question_text: "Its a matter of sad joy" Iillustrates__________
49759.explanation: An oxymoron is a term for a figure of speech. It is made up of two or more words that seem to be opposite to each other, or actually are opposite.

49760.subject: Literature in English
49760.question_text: The leading character in a literary work is the________
49760.explanation: A protagonist (from Ancient Greek πρωταγωνιστής (protagonistes), meaning 'one who plays the first part, chief actor') is the leading character of a story. Theprotagonist is at the center of the story, makes the key decisions, and experiences the consequences of those decisions.

49825.subject: Literature in English
49825.question_text: A narrative poem that relates heroic exploits is an___________
49825.explanation: In literature, an epic is a long narrative poem, which is usually related to heroic deeds of a person of an unusual courage and unparalleled bravery.

49828.subject: Literature in English
49828.question_text: Over the cobbles it clattered and crashed is an example of__________
49828.explanation: Onomatopoeia is one way a poet can create sounds in a poem

49830.subject: Literature in English
49830.explanation: Conflict is a fundamental element of drama. It drives the plot forward and creates tension and interest for the audience. It can be internal (within a character) or external (between characters or between a character and their environment) and it often leads to the development of characters and themes throughout the play.

49833.subject: Literature in English
49833.question_text: A humorous poem with five lines, the first two ryhming with the last is______________
49833.explanation: A limerick is a humorous poem consisting of five lines. The first, second, and fifth lines must have seven to ten syllables while rhyming and having the same verbal rhythm. The third and fourth lines only have to have five to seven syllables, and have to rhyme with each other and have the same rhythm.

49837.subject: Literature in English
49837.question_text: Death be not proud, though some have called thee might and dreadful is an example of___________

49839.subject: Literature in English
49839.question_text: An essential part of the plot is____________
49839.explanation:
The plot of a literary work is the sequence of events in a story. An essential part of the plot is the exposition, which:

  • Introduces the setting

  • Presents the main characters

  • Provides the background information necessary for understanding the story

Without exposition, the reader would not clearly understand who, where, when and what the story is about.

49841.subject: Literature in English
49841.question_text: The climax in a literary work is the_____________
49841.explanation: The climax or turning point of a narrative work is its point of highest tension and drama, or it is the time when the action starts during which the solution is given. The climax of a story is a literary element.

49846.subject: Literature in English
49846.explanation: The characters in a play are sometimes referred to as thedramatis personae.

49848.subject: Literature in English
49848.question_text: Ten thousand saw i at glance....... Illustrates_________
49848.explanation: Hyperbole, from a Greek word meaning "excess," is a figure of speech that uses extreme exaggeration to make a point or show emphasis. It is the opposite of understatement.

49850.subject: Literature in English
49850.explanation: Catharsis, the purification or purgation of the emotions (especially pity and fear) primarily through art. ... Aristotle states that the purpose of tragedy is to arouse “terror and pity” and thereby effect the catharsis of these emotions.

49858.subject: Literature in English
49858.question_text: The dominant feeling in the passage is that of______________
49858.explanation: The passage conveys a strong sense of unease and fear. The narrator describes a turbulent night with disturbing events, including the strange cry "non-indigenes must go" and the unsettling silence of the parents. These elements suggest that the family is worried and fearful about their safety, and this creates a dominant feeling of anxiety throughout the passage. While the strange cry of "non-indigines must go" portrays signs of hostility, this is not the dominant feeling in the passage; the dominant one is one of fear and anxiety in the face of the uncertainty of the family's safety.

49862.subject: Literature in English
49862.question_text: The feeling is conveyed by the use of_________

49865.subject: Literature in English
49865.explanation:
The expression “Their silence spoke millions” combines two contradictory ideas:

  • Silence → absence of speech

  • Spoke → act of speaking

Putting these opposing ideas together creates an oxymoron, a common literary device used to convey deep meaning through contrast. Here, it suggests that although the parents said nothing, their silence communicated fear and danger very powerfully.

49867.subject: Literature in English
49867.question_text: The family bell summoned us is an example of__________
49867.explanation: Personification is a literary device in which non-human objects or abstract concepts are given human qualities or characteristics. In the given sentence, the family bell is described as if it has the human ability to summon people. Since a bell doesn't actually have the ability to summon, this is an example of personification.

49873.subject: Literature in English
49873.explanation:
A tercet is a stanza made up of three lines.

The first stanza of the poem is:

I know not, Amina
When again on your brightness of smile
My eyes will rest awhile

This stanza clearly contains three lines, so it is a tercet.
